global-dollar-currencies::dollar-yoy.title: Broad Dollar Index · year-over-year
global-dollar-currencies::dollar-yoy.why: The broad dollar's year-over-year move, scored two-sided on magnitude: a surging dollar squeezes the world's dollar borrowers and a sliding one imports inflation, so both raise severity. Under ~5% is normal drift.

global-dollar-currencies::euro.title: Euro · dollars per euro
global-dollar-currencies::euro.note: A market price has no inherent good-or-bad level — higher or lower isn't itself better or worse.

global-growth::world-growth.title: World Real GDP Growth · annual
global-growth::world-growth.why: Annual world real-GDP growth, scored against its long-run trend of about 3.5%. Below roughly 2% is what economists call a global recession; the bands step down from trend toward that line.

global-growth::china-growth.title: China Real GDP Growth · annual
global-growth::china-growth.note: Shown for context alongside this lens's lead growth reading.

global-growth::ea-gdp-quarterly.title: Euro Area Real GDP · year-over-year
global-growth::ea-gdp-quarterly.why: Scored on the year-over-year change where FALLING is the stress signal — profits, new-business applications, capital-goods orders, sales. Growth is ok; the bands mark progressively deeper contractions.

global-trade-supply::gscpi.title: Global Supply Chain Pressure Index
global-trade-supply::gscpi.why: The NY Fed supply-chain pressure index, in standard deviations from normal. Negative is looser than normal (ok); the bands climb toward extreme disruption (the COVID peak was about 4.5σ).

global-trade-supply::trade-balance.title: U.S. Trade Deficit · goods & services
global-trade-supply::trade-balance.note: The U.S. has run a trade deficit every year since 1976 — the level isn't good or bad on its own; what matters is the trend shown here.

global-trade-supply::import-prices.title: Import Prices · year-over-year
global-trade-supply::import-prices.why: A cost already expressed as a year-over-year rate. Same logic as the fuel costs: faster annual increases mean more household strain; flat or falling is ok.

global-trade-supply::china-exports.title: China Exports · year-over-year
global-trade-supply::china-exports.note: Shown for context — a noisy global-demand pulse the lens's scored indicators read more cleanly.

global-uncertainty::us-epu.title: U.S. Economic Policy Uncertainty
global-uncertainty::us-epu.why: The Baker/Bloom/Davis policy-uncertainty index, whose long-run norm is about 100, so the bands mark multiples of that norm. The global index (GEPU) is held to a 'watch' ceiling here, because it publishes about six months late — too stale to drive a live alarm.
